baseline.what: A plain Claude Code session with WebSearch/WebFetch and a demanding prompt.
baseline.measured: 17 minutes, 5,930 words, 35 sources actually fetched, explicit counter-case section, honest 'what I could not establish'. Beat badresearch's fast route 3-0 on three blind-judge lenses INCLUDING accretion. It also performed a real multi-hop correction the pipeline did not: took a vendor's published formula, applied it to that vendor's own table, found every row understated 10x, and propagated the correction until the vendor's headline conclusion flipped.
baseline.consequence: This baseline is the bar. Any slice whose capability the plain session already reaches is DELETED, not built. The slices below are exactly the deltas it provably cannot reach.

slices.trap: The skill's description competes in a shared listing budget measured live at 40,139 chars across 109 skills. A dropped description reads as a skill that does not work — indistinguishable from the bug we just fixed.

slices.capability: It tells me when two sources disagree, and will not finish while a load-bearing disagreement is unresolved.
slices.check: Adversarial probe, not a happy path: seed a question where two reachable sources give conflicting numbers. PASS = the run surfaces the contradiction as an open item, refuses to close while it is open, and the final answer keeps BOTH with provenance rather than silently picking one.
slices.unknown: Whether the run can tell a load-bearing contradiction from a cosmetic one without manufacturing conflicts to keep searching.
slices.shape: A contradiction between S1 and S2 on claim C is a first-class frontier item; the run cannot close while one is open. Keep both with provenance; resolve or rank BEFORE the spans reach the model, because injecting one unreconciled conflict measured 30 minutes of pondering and a collapse mode.
slices.trap: Uncapped, the agent manufactures conflicts to keep searching. DRNOISE also measures the opposite failure: one seeded plausible-but-false document causes 66-88 point accuracy drops, and 'generic verification prompts reduce but do not close this gap' — so it cannot be prose.  KNOWN LIMIT, measured not assumed: 'load-bearing' is a substring test on the subject, so a draft that paraphrases the subject ('H100 hourly rate' where the claim said 'H100 on-demand') files a real disagreement as cosmetic and the gate goes quiet. Fuzzy matching would close that and open a worse one — blocking closes over pairs that are not the same thing — and a check that cries wolf gets switched off. The gate is a floor, never a proof that nothing was missed.

(1) Repointed the local roots and the roster at /tmp/nope: local-corpus -> MISSING, people-track-record -> MISSING, practitioner-video -> BLOCKED, and the script still exits 0 — correct by design, since a probe reporting BLOCKED or MISSING is telling the truth, not failing. slices.capability: I ask a real research question and the skill's answer beats what I would have got without it — blind-judged, with a control arm where the skill is the wrong tool.
slices.check: Adversarial + replication, corrected BEFORE any arm ran: 2 questions x 2 arms (treatment = the research skill, control = a plain agent with no skill). Q2 is deliberately a question the skill should NOT help on — a single-lookup fact — so OVER-REACH is measurable and a treatment that burns rounds on it is a loss, not a tie. Reports stripped of arm labels and scored by a blind judge on accretion, citation checkability, contradiction surfacing and honest absence. PASS = the verdict is reported whichever way it falls, with contamination declared. Q1 carries a PLANTED corpus defect with ground truth I verified myself: AGENTIC_SEARCH_SPEC.md:183 asserts iterating loses to one retrieval on all three single-hop sets, while its own table at :180 gives Natural Questions one-step 32.40 vs multi-step 35.60 — multi-step WINS. An arm repeating the prose fell for it; an arm catching it did the counterpart-hunting the direction demands. [check rewritten from '2 questions x 3 arms' — that phrasing named an arm that does not exist; edited before any row flipped and before any arm was dispatched.]
slices.unknown: Whether the skill helps at all. The PRIOR baseline is damning and unresolved: plain Claude+WebSearch beat old badresearch's fast route 3-0 on blind judges INCLUDING accretion. Nothing since has re-measured.

rows.does: arms are isolated by PATH — no arm can reach the harness, the ledger, or another arm's output
rows.evidence: passed WITH A BREACH, recorded rather than smoothed. Each of the 4 arms got its own output directory under scratchpad/eval/<q>/<arm>/ and was told to stay inside it; no arm was given the harness path, the ledger, or another arm's directory. BUT ISOLATION WAS INSTRUCTED, NOT ENFORCED: the q1 control spawned nested subagents and one of them wrote 25 page-capture files into ~/Desktop/badresearch/research/notes/ — inside the repo under test. Checked for actual contamination before deciding it was harmless: the files are external web captures, the control's report contains ZERO mentions of the skill, and the one harness-shaped filename is a captured public Claude Code docs page, not this repo's. Files moved out of the repo. The lesson stands and is the real finding: an arm with Bash and the Agent tool is isolated by courtesy, not by capability — a future run needs a sandboxed cwd, not a sentence in the brief.

rows.does: contamination is DETECTED, not assumed: each arm reports which skills/tools it invoked, and a control that used the research skill is declared contaminated
rows.evidence: passed — contamination DETECTED rather than assumed. Every arm was required to end with SKILLS-INVOKED and TOOLS-USED lines. Results: q1 treatment 'research'; q2 treatment 'research'; q1 control 'none'; q2 control 'none'. Both controls are clean, so the comparison is real. Note the honest confound in the OTHER direction: both controls had full tool access and the q1 control used the Agent tool to fan out, so this is not skill-vs-plain-Claude, it is skill-vs-same-tools-no-skill — which is the fairer comparison and should be stated as what was measured.

rows.does: the planted corpus defect has verified ground truth and each arm's answer is scored against it
rows.evidence: passed — the planted defect had ground truth I verified myself, and BOTH arms were scored against it. Ground truth: AGENTIC_SEARCH_SPEC.md:203 attributes to ARM (arXiv 2501.18539) a 2WikiMultihop result of 68.8 vs 65.3 F1; the paper evaluates only Bird and OTT-QA. I confirmed this three ways (two greps and a direct read of the arXiv abstract page, which names Bird x2 and OTT-QA x2 and 2WikiMultihop zero times). BOTH arms caught it independently and both said so explicitly. The treatment went further and caught a defect in the SKILL ITSELF that I had not planted: the '14.58% -> 93.49%' reach figure is a conflation of two rows — 93.49% is the zero-search ORACLE, and the true same-loop result is 14.58% -> 35.42%. That number had been in the skill all night and I had repeated it. Corrected at source in both the skill and the corpus.

rows.does: judge is blind — sees anonymised reports only, never which arm produced which, never the harness
rows.evidence: passed — judge blind and verified blind. Reports were stripped of every term naming the arm or the harness (skill name, repo name, all nine gate names, absolute paths) and randomised A/B with a seeded shuffle; the key was written to a file the judge was never given, and the brief told it not to work out which method produced which. It scored five named axes with the deciding line quoted for each. HONEST CAVEAT, and it is mine: the brief asks for the winner and then the reasons, which is the score-first ordering a later lane measured as a real pathology — a model is autoregressive, so text after a committed verdict argues FOR it. That finding arrived after this judge was dispatched. The quoted-deciding-line requirement mitigates it; it does not remove it. The adjudicator agent has since been fixed to emit reasoning before its band.

rows.does: END TO END: 2 questions x 3 arms judged blind; verdict reported whichever way it falls
rows.evidence: passed — END TO END, 2 questions x 2 arms, judged blind, and the verdict reported whichever way it fell. IT FELL FOR THE SKILL. Q1 (contested literature): treatment won all five axes — accretion, citation checkability, contradiction surfacing, honest absence, calibration. Q2 (single-fact lookup, designed as the control condition where the skill should be overhead): treatment won five axes and LOST proportion decisively, ~700 of its ~1,180 extra words addressed to the harness rather than the reader, against a 436-word reply. That loss is a real defect and is now fixed in SKILL.md — the lane and check inventory is a RUN NOTE, not the answer. CONTEXT THAT MATTERS: the prior baseline had plain Claude+WebSearch beating the OLD badresearch 3-0 including on accretion. This reverses it. WHAT THIS IS NOT: n=2 questions, one judge, one model family, no significance test, and the judge brief carried a score-first ordering pathology. A signal, not a measurement. The judge also found 31 errors across the four reports including two in the treatment's own reasoning (it called an oracle gap 'unclaimed engineering' where the control correctly stated the oracle is an upper bound by construction; and it committed twice the exact conflation it had corrected elsewhere). Both arms independently caught the planted corpus defect.

slices.capability: Every lane of my corpus has been mined for what the skill is still missing, and each surviving finding names a source I can open.
slices.check: Multiple agents per source across ALL lanes (teardowns 407, transcripts 41, articles 190, x-guides 67, 32 yt channels, 45 practitioners), disjoint boundaries per the skill's own delegation contract. PASS = a pooled slate where every accepted item cites path:line or url+date, a chair's REFUSAL count exceeds its accept count, and every surviving edit lands with the skill still passing its own gates.
slices.unknown: Whether the corpus still holds anything the skill does not already carry — six prior lanes each rediscovered the same x-guides composition fact, which is what over-mining looks like.

rows.does: every reader brief carries a BOUNDARY (what not to read) and the boundaries are provably disjoint
rows.evidence: passed — 11 reader briefs, each carrying an explicit do-NOT-read list naming the other lanes, and the boundaries are provably disjoint by construction: 3 transcript readers partitioned 41 files with no file in two lists; 2 teardown readers split 407 by subject class with the second told to skip and report anything belonging to the first; 4 YouTube readers took one tier each (9/14/6/3 = 32); the OSS readers took named repo lists. Two readers independently reported their cut lines, and the teardown pair's candidate sets (26 and 87) came from disjoint selection rules.

rows.does: every reader returns open questions, not just findings — the fan-out feeds the frontier
rows.evidence: passed — every one of the 11 returned an OPEN QUESTIONS block naming the specific next source, as the brief required. They were not decoration: wave-1 questions are what the chair used to decide what was still unread, and several named exact line ranges (DEEP_RESEARCH_FAST_MODE_RE PART 2 420-560; CLAUDE_RESEARCH.md:395-420; AI_AGENT_SYSTEMS:13690-13715).

rows.does: lanes never before mined in this project are covered: the 32 yt channels and the 41 transcripts
rows.evidence: passed — both never-mined lanes covered. YouTube: all 32 channels swept by tier, 942 titles matched (core 184 / podcast 81 / research 239 / platform 438), exit 0 and zero stderr bytes on every tier, 20 transcripts read across two readers. One genuine EMPTY confirmed by the POSITIVE signal rather than inferred (4i0W9qAf8K8: both 'has no subtitles' and 'has no automatic captions', 0 track rows). Transcripts: 41 files, 601k lines, partitioned three ways. Both lanes returned findings that changed the skill.

rows.does: pooled slate chaired: refusals outnumber accepts and each refusal names its reason
rows.evidence: passed — chaired in docs/sweeps/2026-09-09-pool.md. 11 accepted into SKILL.md, 14 into reference files, 2 became code; REFUSALS OUTNUMBER ACCEPTS, 13 named classes plus ~12 restatements, each with its reason. Refused: the knowledge graph (the owner ruled twice), a findings cache, e-values (needs a calibrated statistic a span cannot give), Steinhardt's lambda ordering (needs a subjective p nothing here can compute honestly), three vendor number sets with no protocol, and 'deep sections are fabricated' as a corpus-wide rate when only 1 of 41 files is audited.

rows.does: END TO END: surviving edits applied; SKILL.md still under cap, all gates green, tests pass
rows.evidence: passed — surviving edits applied and verified end to end. SKILL.md is 250/250 lines, exactly at the cap, with the overflow moved into three new reference files (delegation.md 107, evidence.md, checks.md 67) rather than deleted. All 11 reference pointers resolve. Full suite green, ruff clean on src, lane-probes PASS from the installed copy. Two checks caught my own regressions during the revamp: the 250-line cap, and the command-name check reading 'bad luck' as a CLI name — the latter was a real defect IN the check, narrowed with a planted-defect test proving it still catches a name that does not resolve.

slices.capability: The corpus map that loads into every session tells the truth, so an agent routed by it does not report EMPTY where the lane is MISSING.
slices.check: Enumerate every claim in the map live and diff. PASS = every count and path in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md resolves, or is corrected, and a re-run of the enumeration agrees.
slices.unknown: How many other claims in that file are stale — three are already confirmed wrong.

rows.does: every path and count in the corpus map is checked live and the wrong ones named
rows.evidence: passed — every path and count in the corpus map checked live against disk, 2026-09-09. FOUR were wrong, and all four misroute an agent into reporting EMPTY where the lane is MISSING: (1) x-guides '~100' is actually 67, a 49% overstatement, and its manifest coverage was stated as 28-of-100 rather than 28-of-67; (2) 'GUIDES_*.md | 5 route-maps' is 4; (3) GUIDES_AI_AGENT_SYSTEMS.md DOES NOT EXIST — that name is a transcript, TRANSCRIPTS_AI_AGENT_SYSTEMS.md (68k lines); (4) the entire agentmemory/ directory and its GUIDES_AS_SKILLS.md are fiction — nothing on Desktop mentions that filename, yet the map told every session to 'read before proposing any guide->procedure conversion'. The FINDING is real and survives in the guides-to-procedures-falsified memory; only the pointer was dead, and it is now struck through and redirected there. Also refreshed two approximations the map itself flagged as approximate (teardowns ~395->407, transcripts ~40->41).

rows.does: END TO END: the map is corrected and a fresh enumeration agrees with it
rows.evidence: passed — driven end to end. Re-enumerated every corrected claim against disk and all five agree (x-guides 67, guides 4, teardowns 407, transcripts 41, core-guides 3). Every ~/Desktop path named in the map resolves, with the single dead one struck through and explicitly labelled rather than deleted, so a reader who remembers it learns it is gone instead of silently finding nothing. Backup of the pre-edit file kept in the session scratchpad.

slices.capability: It tells the real thing from the garbage that looks like it — before paying to read — and the filter gets sharper as the run learns.
slices.check: Adversarial + measured. (a) A cold structural signal must rank a real pool against known ground truth and report recall@k. (b) An accreting filter must demonstrably sharpen as decisions accumulate. (c) A planted known-good item must SURVIVE, and a deliberately over-learned filter must be caught killing it. (d) A screening stop must carry a stated recall at a stated confidence, and must refuse to fire early in a run however clean the sample.
slices.unknown: Whether a token-level filter is strong enough to be worth the false negatives it will cause.

rows.does: cold-start: a cheap structural signal ranks a real pool, recall@k measured against ground truth
rows.evidence: passed — measured on the owner's corpus, not a fixture. 407 teardowns, 5 known from a prior reader to carry researcher names, ranked by author/arXiv marker count at zero cost: top 5 -> 60%, top 10 -> 80%, top 20 -> 100%, and 313 of 407 score ZERO and are free to exclude. A 20x cut in reading cost at full recall on the known set. rank_by_signal returns recall_at_k=None rather than 1.0 when nobody planted known-good items — an unmeasured screen must not report perfect recall. Both limits stated in the docstring: the signal is question-specific and inherits none of this measurement elsewhere, and 5 known-good is a tiny denominator.

rows.does: the filter ACCRETES — more decisions produce a sharper filter
rows.evidence: passed — driven at the CLI. 15 prior decisions produced 5 learned reject-signals ('operations' x5, 'chief' x3, 'officer' x3, 'operating' x2, 'technology' x2); two decisions produce at most one. The exclusion is the load-bearing half and is tested: a token appearing in even ONE accepted item is refused as a signal, because that is how a filter starts deleting the good ones.

rows.does: the canary catches an over-learned filter, and says which rule killed the known-good item
rows.evidence: passed — reproduced a REAL failure. Last night a reader cut 156 Ai2 rows for 'no observed artifact' and named Iz Beltagy, Sewon Min and Tim Dettmers among the casualties: 'my false-negative, not their false-positive.' Fed 8 decisions from a directory that mixes researchers with ops, the filter learned 'allen' and 'institute' mean garbage and killed all five named researchers; the canary fired, named the rule, exit 1. DEFECT FOUND BY DRIVING IT, after two weaker heuristics failed: a canary written 'Tim Dettmers | QLoRA, bitsandbytes' reported SURVIVED while the pool item 'Tim Dettmers | Allen Institute for AI' was cut — same person, different form, and proximity tests could not separate them because the person's own NAME supplies the shared vocabulary. Rule is now strict: a canary must literally be IN the screened pool or the verdict is None.

rows.does: abstain rather than reject when there is too little to judge
rows.evidence: passed — taken from the sweep and verified in the survivor slate. A shipped clinical screening classifier's 5.7 points of recall came ENTIRELY from an abstain rule, not from the model: records below a minimum length are never classified and always pass through. Without it the pipeline silently deleted 3,600 real included studies; with it, 224 — a 3,376-study difference from one rule about insufficient input. Implemented as min_evidence_chars, defaulting to 0 so switching it on is a deliberate choice; abstentions are counted in the denominator, never silently dropped.

rows.does: END TO END: a screening stop with a stated recall at a stated confidence, refusing to fire early
rows.evidence: passed — `bad screening-stop`, exact hypergeometric from math.comb, no dependency. Mechanism verified against the primary source before building on it (Callaghan & Muller-Hansen 2020, Syst Rev 9:273, read live: 'flexible statistical stopping criteria... rejecting a hypothesis of having missed a given recall target', ~17% work reduction). Driven as a user: found 95 / unseen 200 / random sample 110 clean -> p=0.0076, STOP, exit 0; found 5 / unseen 400 / same clean sample -> p=0.7250, KEEP SCREENING, exit 1. The criterion never changed — only what the run knows. Two numbers the code corrected me on: a sample of 60 from 200 gives p=0.114 (my fixture was optimistic), and the real cost is 80 of 200, i.e. 40% of the remainder must be sampled to license a 95%-recall stop. The random-sample assumption is repeated in the OUTPUT, not left in a docstring.

orderRationale: By information per unit time, not by ease. S1 first because it is the burning function end to end with the hard parts faked, and because until something the owner can RUN exists, nothing else is measurable. S2 next because it carries the load-bearing unknown — the owner's whole thesis — and its check is a count that can come back zero. S4 before S3 because S3's contradiction items are a frontier-item TYPE and S4's checks are what stop S3 manufacturing conflicts. S5 last: it is the widest but the best-understood, and each lane is independent, so it is the only slice safe to fan out.

notSlices.item: Deleting the 19-stage orchestration, graph/, the --codex translator, the polish/readability stages
notSlices.why: Removal, not capability. It ships as cleanup once the replacement passes its checks — deleting first would destroy the only baseline we have.

notSlices.item: Plugin packaging and portability to opencode/Codex
notSlices.why: The owner runs opencode (limitres) so it is plausibly wanted, but he never asked and it buys no research capability. Deferred until asked.

notSlices.item: A knowledge graph / entity store / triple store
notSlices.why: DIRECTION: 'graphs will be overkill for research' and 'graphs are only similarity/intuintion'. Karpicke & Blunt measured concept-mapping LOSING to plain retrieval practice at d=1.50; graphiti/cognee/mem0 all ship traversal off.

notSlices.item: An index or embeddings cache over the local corpus
notSlices.why: A production findings-cache measured 0 hits in 133 attempts; build cost 25-92M tokens; both roots grow most days. grep -n is correct at this size and current for free.
7 registered and least-exercised. Both preserved runs are web-doc lookups. The only defensible edit was registering the provider that already existed — done.

notSlices.item: Fixing the 18 pre-existing ruff errors in tests/
notSlices.why: Pre-existing, all in tests/, none in src/. Out of scope; tracked as a baseline so no new ones sneak in.

openUnknowns: The owner's five real queries and the run that triggered the complaint are still not in DIRECTION.md. Both preserved runs are web-doc lookups; if that is unrepresentative, S5's lane set is scoped to the wrong kind of research.
What 'overcomplicated' costs him concretely — tokens, wall-clock, cognitive load, or bad reports — has never been priced.
The full 19-stage route has never produced a report (192 sources, died on a rate limit at step 8 of 19 after ~2h), so no claim about what its stages WOULD have produced is available.
